inventory-packing.context: An online sales team with several packers and customer-service staff processes daily orders from two marketplaces.
inventory-packing.problem: Orders, stock, and packing were managed in many spreadsheets: separate tabs per packer, packing recaps, and stock notes built by hand. It was hard to see which goods to prepare that day, which SKUs were running low, and who was working on which order.
inventory-packing.solution: A multi-tenant inventory platform. Orders arrive through a marketplace API or a CSV/Excel import, the system builds the day's goods requirement and splits orders across packers, and each packer receives a digital packing sheet on their phone. Stock drops automatically when packing is confirmed through a mutation log that is never edited, stock status (safe, careful, use up, empty) is calculated automatically, and each seller's data is isolated with row-level security.

internal-automation.context: A creator agency tracks the performance of TikTok videos from partner creators. Before this, an automated workflow wrote the results to Google Sheets.
internal-automation.problem: Video performance was tracked in a spreadsheet filled by a workflow, with no dedicated view to filter by creator or month, read comments, group by campaign, or limit access between team members.
internal-automation.solution: The internal team pastes up to 50 video links per submission. The app stores them under a campaign and a batch, then calls an n8n workflow that splits the links into groups of 25, fetches the metrics through a third-party scraper, computes the engagement rate, and writes the result to the database. Progress shows live with an estimated finish time, and videos that fail (private or deleted) are logged per batch. The dashboard offers a table that can be searched, filtered, sorted, and exported to CSV, a comments panel, a trend chart, and five prompt templates for AI analysis. Two-level access (super admin and admin) is protected in layers through row-level security, middleware, and column-level grants.

n8n workflow fetches metrics for each video
Results and errors are logged, progress shows live
Team filters, exports, and analyses with AI

internal-automation.learning: Access protection should be layered: a leftover page file once became a way around the role check at the application layer. So the restriction is also set in the database (row-level security) and in column-level grants, not only in the app.

content-partner-platform.context: A team that manages marketplace affiliate creators needs one place for products, tutorial material, and the webinar schedule.
content-partner-platform.solution: A role-based web app with three modules: products, tutorials (with learning-progress tracking), and a webinar schedule (with attendance records). Two-layer login: internal accounts through OAuth and creators through an ID and password, with row-level security for three roles. Two n8n workflows fetch product images automatically and send a daily webinar reminder.
